title: Error Annotation Railroad — compact payload annotation rail for fast triage
creator: Jonah Reed
description: Problem: Investigating failed requests in the Console is slow when engineers must hop between long JSON payloads, raw logs, and isolated metadata panels. Context loss occurs during repeated retries and when comparing near-identical payload versions. Goal: Design a compact, horizontal 'annotation railroad' — a lightweight, scrollable timeline strip that summarizes a request's retry history, error taxonomy, and inline payload annotations. The railroad sits above the full payload view and provides quick jump points, inline diffs, and integrated error tags so triage is fast without losing access to full fidelity payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Rail displays one row-per-attempt with timestamp, error-tag (taxonomy), latency, and delta-badge when payload changed
Clicking a rail node opens the full payload snapshot anchored to the same scroll position
Inline diff glyphs indicate token-level or key/value changes and open a micro-diff panel on hover
Filters available: error taxonomy, retry-status (succeeded/failed/timeout), time window, and user-labels
Prototype tested with 6 engineers and achieves median time-to-first-action reduction >=30% vs current flow
decisions: Keep railroad lightweight: render minimal metadata inline and lazy-load full payload on node selection to preserve Console perf
Prioritize key/value structured diffs for typical JSON payloads; show token-level diffs only when size < 500 tokens to avoid clutter
Use existing error taxonomy tags (ENG-9211) rather than inventing new labels to maintain cross-team consistency
Expose a compact 'copy snapshot' CTA on each node for quick repro steps — chosen over auto-download to avoid accidental data exfiltration

ux_notes: Rail nodes are 52px tall on desktop; tooltip on hover shows full timestamp + request-id
Use condensed typography for long keys; show ellipsis with hover-to-expand in the payload panel
Keyboard: left/right to move between attempts, Enter to open full payload, D to open diff mode
Mobile: railroad collapses into a stacked list with sticky summary for current attempt
usability_findings: Users prefer a horizontal scrubber when comparing near-identical retries rather than vertical scrolling
Micro-diff hover reduced cognitive load vs opening separate diffs for many users
Privacy concerns require explicit redaction and audit logs when snapshots are revealed
